newsitem.title: UK: EBRD's de Larosiere not sure whether to stay on.
newsitem.headline: EBRD's de Larosiere not sure whether to stay on.

text.p: Jacques de Larosiere said on Wednesday he had not decided whether to stay on as president of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) when his term expires later this year.

De Larosiere took over the Bank in 1993 when it was better known for its costly marbled headquarters in London that for fulfilling its role in helping the newly emerging East Bloc countries in their transition to market economies.
"I still need more time (to decide)," he told a news conference.
His current four-year term expires this September.
Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn, representing the Bank's shareholders, two weeks ago asked him whether he would be prepared to continue in the job.
"It was a very touching manifestation of their confidence...(but) I was not yet in a position to give an answer...I will make up my mind in the coming months," he said.
There would be no decision by the time the Bank holds its annual meeting next month in London, he added.

Former head of the International Monetary Fund and governor of the Bank of France, de Larosiere was brought in to replace Jacques Attali, the first president, who had been criticised for his spending on the Bank's head office.
Under de Larosiere's rule, the Bank has sharply increased its activities in eastern Europe, now covering 26 countries, as well as cut costs.
Last year, he managed to persuade wealthy nations to pump an extra $20 billion into the Bank's capital.
